rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the main flow reaches a defined end outcome, and then names a later occurrence from an outside party that may lead to additional handling: Do not model that later occurrence as a start event with no incoming flow that opens its own chain to an end event. Model it either as an event subprocess (triggeredByEvent=true, exactly one triggered start event, no sequence flows), as a separate process, or as a catch branch joined to the main flow through a gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the main flow reaches a defined end outcome, and then names a later occurrence from an outside party that may lead to additional handling

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process is started by an external participant who can perform the initiating action through one of several alternative channels, each described as a distinct action: Model a single start event with no incoming flow. Model each alternative channel as its own bpmn:task in the pool or lane of the external participant who performs it. Place an exclusive split after the start event that leads to these tasks, and join them with an exclusive merge before the organization's first internal activity. Do not merge the alternatives into one generic task or drop a channel that the description names.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process is started by an external participant who can perform the initiating action through one of several alternative channels, each described as a distinct action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the process ends once a completion step has been carried out successfully, and that a later occurrence (such as feedback or a return) may follow after the end: Model the completion step as its own task on the main flow, placed directly before a single end event. Name the end event for the process end, not for the outcome. Model the later occurrence as a separate task or branch that is joined to the main flow through a gateway, and do not fold it into the label of the end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the process ends once a completion step has been carried out successfully, and that a later occurrence (such as feedback or a return) may follow after the end

rules_sent_back.instruction: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the process ends at a terminal outcome, and that a later occurrence from outside the main flow (such as customer feedback or a return) may lead to follow-up work after that end

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process begins when an actor performs one of several alternative actions (for example placing an order through one channel or another), and no single event itself starts the process: Model one start event for the process. Model each alternative action as its own task that follows the start event, and merge these alternative tasks with an exclusive gateway before the next activity. Do not model the actor's alternative actions as separate start events, and do not omit them from the model.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process begins when an actor performs one of several alternative actions (for example placing an order through one channel or another), and no single event itself starts the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a process begins when an external party performs one of several alternative actions, each through a different channel, and the organization's response is the same whichever channel is used: Model each alternative channel as its own start event with no incoming flow, and let every such start event lead into the same first internal task of the process. Do not collapse the alternative channels into one generic start event with no trace of the channel, and do not model the external action itself as a task performed by the organization.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a process begins when an external party performs one of several alternative actions, each through a different channel, and the organization's response is the same whichever channel is used

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the main work of the process ends once a completion step is done, and then says that a later occurrence from an external party (such as a reply or a return) may lead to additional work: Do not give the later occurrence its own start event with a separate chain to its own end event inside the same process. Keep one main flow with one end event. Route the later occurrence into that main flow through a gateway placed before the end event, or model it as an event subprocess or as a separate process. Every start event in the process must lead into the main flow or into a clearly separate process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the main work of the process ends once a completion step is done, and then says that a later occurrence from an external party (such as a reply or a return) may lead to additional work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity together with its recipient, its completion endpoint, or a second action coordinated with it (for example 'generates ... and sends it to the recipient', or 'sends ... to the recipient', or 'monitors ... until a stated condition'): Name the task so that its label keeps every element the description attaches to that activity: the recipient, the endpoint or completion condition, and any coordinated second action. Use the description's verbs and the qualifiers it states, and do not shorten the label to a bare verb-object pair that drops them. Keep the label short, but do not remove a stated part of the action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity together with its recipient, its completion endpoint, or a second action coordinated with it (for example 'generates ... and sends it to the recipient', or 'sends ... to the recipient', or 'monitors ... until a stated condition')
